I am not looking for a therapy conversation, and I am not interested in being told to “practice self-care.” I am trying to keep my job and keep stability for my kids, and I need this to stand up.

Two tracks are running at the same time.

Work: I am dealing with a workplace conflict that has started to look like a pretext. I have been through “informal coaching” that felt like selective enforcement, and I am concerned this becomes a performance improvement plan without any real objective criteria. I have documentation, but it is scattered.

Home: High-conflict co-parenting. There is a custody order with timelines and exchange provisions, and my ex uses school communications to create friction. I keep things controlled, but the volume is constant and it is affecting sleep.

I need a structured approach. If you are going to be useful, start by telling me what inputs you need: what specific policy language, what dates, what categories of documentation, and what the decision tree is when I get provoked—at work or in writing with my ex. I need something workplace-grade, not generic reassurance.

I can do this. Below I’m giving the exact inputs I need, a compact folder/timeline structure, and two short decision trees (work / co‑parent) you can follow in the moment.

What I need from you (exact items)
- Workplace policy excerpts: code of conduct, informal coaching policy, PIP/grievance/appeal procedures (copy the specific sections/paragraph numbers).
- Dates & times: every incident (coaching, meetings, emails), who was present, location, and outcome.
- Documentation types: original emails/screenshots (with headers), meeting notes, coaching notes, performance metrics, witness names, any prior evaluations.
- HR/manager contacts, union rep or attorney info (if any).
- Custody order text: exchange provisions, communication rules, any contempt/enforcement clauses (quote exact language).
- School communications: copies (emails/texts), dates, screenshots, staff names.
- Any police reports, court filings, or formal complaints.

Folder & timeline setup (quick)
- Single spreadsheet timeline (date/time, category, summary, doc link, witnesses).
- Digital folders: /Work/Policies, /Work/Incidents, /Home/CourtOrder, /Home/SchoolMsgs.
- Save originals; export emails to PDF with headers.

Decision tree — workplace (brief)
1) Calm pause. Don’t respond in thread.  
2) Timestamp & log incident. Save original.  
3) If coaching lacks objective criteria → request written criteria and measurable targets; CC HR.  
4) If PIP proposed → demand written PIP with metrics, timeline, evaluation method; ask for meeting and witnesses.  
5) If unfair/retaliatory → escalate to HR/union/attorney with timeline and witnesses.

Decision tree — co‑parent / school messages (brief)
1) Pause. Don’t escalate in kind.  
2) Save original message (PDF/screenshots). Log date/time.  
3) Reply only with factual, minimal language referencing custody order or school policy; CC school admin if needed.  
4) If pattern persists, send a formal notice citing the custody order and request school copy communications to you; then consult attorney for enforcement motion.

If you want, send the first 7–10 dated entries and the custody order/policy excerpts and I’ll draft: (A) a one‑page timeline template and (B) a short, workplace‑grade email templates for (1) requesting objective PIP criteria and (2) responding to provocative school messages.

Understood. Keep it operational.

If this is going to stand up, we need two parallel workstreams with a single evidence spine. Here are the specific inputs I need from you, and the decision trees you asked for.

A) INPUTS I NEED (WORK)
1) Policy language (verbatim excerpts, with section numbers):
- Performance management / PIP policy (trigger criteria, required steps, timelines, appeal rights).
- “Informal coaching” guidance (if it exists) and documentation requirements.
- Anti-retaliation, anti-discrimination, complaint procedure, and investigation standards.
- Any policy on meeting notes, recording, email retention, and expectations/metrics for your role.
2) Your objective job expectations:
- Most recent job description.
- Last 2 performance reviews and any KPI/OKR language.
- Any written goals set for the current cycle.
3) Timeline anchors (dates/times):
- First incident where tone shifted.
- Each coaching meeting: date/time, who attended, what was said, what “expectations” were given.
- Any comparator evidence (others not held to same standard): names/titles (even if you redact), what happened, how management responded.
4) Documentation inventory (what exists and where):
- Emails (export with headers), chat messages, calendar invites.
- Manager/HR notes you received.
- Your contemporaneous notes (even if rough).
- Witness list: who observed what, and whether they would plausibly confirm.

B) INPUTS I NEED (HOME / CO-PARENTING)
1) Custody order excerpts (verbatim):
- Exchange days/times/locations.
- Communication method requirements (email/app), response-time language (if any), and school-communication provisions.
- Any clause on disparagement, interference with school access, or decision-making authority (legal/physical custody).
2) School communication facts:
- Which platform (email, app, school portal), who is included, who is being looped in.
- 5–10 representative messages with dates (you can paste text, remove identifying details).
3) Pattern + impact:
- Volume per week, typical triggers (schedule changes, homework, events, fees), and what “friction” looks like (accusations, administrative complaints, triangulating staff).

C) EVIDENCE SPINE (ONE SYSTEM FOR BOTH)
Create one master timeline spreadsheet with these columns:
- Date/Time
- Track (Work / Co-parent)
- Event type (Meeting / Email / Text / School / Policy / Deadline)
- Summary (2–3 sentences, neutral)
- Source (email header, screenshot filename, calendar invite)
- Who was involved
- What you did in response
- Next deadline / follow-up
Then two folders:
- /WORK/01_Policies 02_Timeline 03_Emails 04_Meetings 05_Performance
- /HOME/01_CourtOrder 02_Timeline 03_School 04_Ex_Communications

D) DECISION TREE WHEN YOU’RE PROVOKED (WORK)
1) Identify the channel: live meeting vs written.
2) Live meeting:
- Do not litigate facts in real time.
- Ask one clarifying question: “What is the objective criterion and how will it be measured?”
- Ask for it in writing: “Please confirm the expectation, metric, and timeline by email.”
- After the meeting, log it the same day.
3) Written provocation (email/chat):
- Pause.
- Save the original.
- Reply only to the actionable item, using neutral language.
- If accusations are included, respond with: “I’m happy to address specific, measurable expectations. Please specify the deliverable, metric, and due date.”
4) Escalation threshold:
- If you see (a) shifting standards, (b) denial of objective metrics, or (c) documentation that contradicts prior reviews, you shift from “operate” to “protect”: consolidate evidence, request HR guidance on process, and stop improvising.

E) DECISION TREE WHEN YOU’RE PROVOKED (CO-PARENT / SCHOOL)
1) Is it time-sensitive for the child (health/safety/same-day logistics)?
- Yes: respond within a short window with facts only.
- No: wait.
2) Reply standard:
- Brief.
- Informative.
- Friendly-neutral.
- Firm.
3) If the message tries to pull you into argument:
- Do not rebut every point.
- Reference the order or school policy once.
- Offer one concrete option and a deadline.
4) Escalation threshold:
- If there is repeated interference with school communication or exchanges, you document patterns by category (missed exchanges, late pickups, school triangulation) and move to a structured notice—one message summarizing the pattern and the specific clause being violated.

F) WHAT I NEED FIRST (TO START BUILDING)
Send me:
1) The exact custody-order clauses on communication and school.
2) Your company’s PIP policy excerpt (or confirm you don’t have access).
3) 7–10 timeline entries (with dates) split across both tracks.
4) One example of a “provocation” email at work and one school-related message from your ex (redact names).

I’m not asking for your life story. I’m asking for the text and the dates. I need this to stand up, so we build from primary-source language and a clean chronology.

2) Company PIP/performance management policy — paste the exact sections (trigger, steps, timelines, appeal/HR process). If you don’t have verbatim, say so.
